title: Analytical Floquet Quantum Statistics from Nonequilibrium Green's Functions
authors: Yuhua Ren, Gaomin Tang, Hui Pan, Jian-Sheng Wang
abstract: We derive an analytical expression for the steady-state quantum statistics of periodically driven quantum systems coupled to a bath using the nonequilibrium Green's function (NEGF) formalism. By embedding Floquet theory into NEGF, we obtain closed expressions for the retarded, advanced, and lesser Green's functions in the Floquet representation, yielding the Floquet Fermi distribution in which the steady-state occupation is expressed as a weighted sum of Fermi functions shifted by integer multiples of the driving frequency. The weights are determined solely by the Fourier components of the micromotion operator, providing a transparent interpretation of Floquet sideband occupations. Our analysis extends beyond the diagonal commuting Hamiltonians treated in earlier work, and further shows that the robust Floquet distribution remains valid for a broad class of weakly coupled bath spectral functions beyond the ideal featureless-bath approximation. Finally, we establish a Floquet version of the Landauer formula for the DC part of the current, in which the equilibrium Fermi functions are replaced by their Floquet-modified counterparts. Together, these results provide a coherent description of Floquet quantum statistics and transport in periodically driven open quantum systems.
summary: This paper develops an analytical method using Nonequilibrium Green's Functions combined with Floquet theory to characterize the steady-state statistics of quantum systems periodically coupled to a bath. It successfully derives the characteristic Floquet Fermi distribution and generalizes fundamental transport relations like the Landauer formula for these driven, open systems.
main_problem: The primary goal is deriving an analytical expression for the steady-state quantum statistics of periodically driven quantum systems coupled to a bath.
main_result: The authors derive the Floquet Fermi distribution, showing that the steady-state occupation is a weighted sum of shifted Fermi functions. They also establish a generalized Landauer formula for DC current in this regime.
method: The work combines Nonequilibrium Green's Function (NEGF) formalism with Floquet theory to handle time-periodic driving and coupling to an environment.
model_or_system: The system consists of a quantum system periodically driven by an external field and coupled to a thermal bath. The analysis is general, extending beyond simple commuting Hamiltonians.
key_observables: Steady-state quantum statistics (occupation distribution), retarded/advanced/lesser Green's functions, and the DC component of the current.
important_parameters: The driving frequency ($\Omega$), temperature ($T$), and the spectral function of the bath are key parameters governing the steady state.
main_assumptions: Assumptions include weak system-bath coupling ($\Gamma 	o 0^+$) and utilizing the Floquet representation to manage time dependence, though extensions beyond ideal baths are shown.
paper_structure: The paper builds a coherent description by first embedding Floquet theory into NEGF, deriving closed-form expressions for Green's functions in the Floquet basis. It then applies this to determine the steady-state statistics and finally generalizes transport formulas like Landauer's.
why_interesting: This work provides a rigorous, unified theoretical framework connecting time-periodic driving (Floquet engineering) directly to non-equilibrium statistical mechanics for open quantum systems, which is highly relevant for understanding driven nanoscale devices.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. Schematic of the system-bath coupling for a hypo- thetical system with NS = 3 states and a bath with 15 states. The bath depicted is composed of three identical sub-baths, with each containing five levels. Each system level couples exclusively and fully to one sub-bath. In the ideal bath as- sumption, both the coupling strength and the sub-bath den- sity of states are uniform.

FIG. 2. Heatmaps of the Floquet Fermi function (Eq. (65)) at temperatures (a) 3 K and (b) 300 K corresponding to a simple sinusoidal driving (Eq. (64)) with frequency ℏΩ= 207 meV. The horizontal axis denotes the equilibrium energy level, while the vertical axis denotes (half of) the modulation amplitude. When ε1 = 0, which corresponds to a vanishing driving amplitude, the system is in equilibrium. A stronger drive widens the boundary between populated (low energy) and unpopulated (high energy) regions. At higher tempera- tures, temperature smearing smooths out the staircase feature of the Floquet Fermi function.

The same sinusoidal resonant level model is used, with Hamilto- nian given by Eq. (64). The Hamiltonian parameters are ℏΩ= 2.07 eV, ϵ0 = 0 eV, and ϵ1 = 372 meV.
